restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 ranges over the whole class of eta (524,288 values; no sub-class, no rule on h1), and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of proof.md Section 8 for the six listed E1 outcomes S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0 are searched further (share 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782), only those that the exact s-pattern pre-check keeps reach the joint solver, and (G7) fixes bit 7 before traversal; by Lemmas F, VP and G7 none loses a counted success. Successes with the eight other outcomes of beta* are not counted. Heuristic part: a search over 2^90.465 walked trials (2^69.465 outer steps of 2^21) for one whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits agree succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under H1', H4' and H5'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 64 registers, immediate constants; each fetch of a memory word costs one load. Outer steps run seven to a batch in lean packed 36-bit lanes: 423 units per batch, 35 per lane whose test-(2) mask meets S, 461 per passing lane (rebuild, pre-check, (G7) stores and credit test included), and for a step the pre-check keeps the proved cap C(T) <= 31,456 of the solver with (G7) (proof.md 9.4, 9.7) and root certificates, debited from a credit of 3,795,525,293,015,084,470,051 units before the solver runs: proved upper allowances of a specified layout, not measured counts. No sorting, no lookup by value, no table that grows with the trials. The run halts with failure when the test-(2) or pass count exceeds its budget, when C(T) exceeds the credit, or after RUN_BATCHES batches; budgets are charged at budget plus one and the solver at the whole credit, so the bound holds on every run (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

Randomized by eight fresh uniform 256-bit words per batch of seven outer steps; each outer step reads its own disjoint bits (proof.md Lemma PL), so the outer steps are independent with the law of one drawn alone. Success 0.39 holds only under H1', H4' and H5'. The factor 98,937,639,497 in H1' is five sevenths of the model's conditional count of the six listed outcomes on the class, rounded down, and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11): no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. The filter, pre-check and (G7) are exact; the shares of the two counts enter only the budgets (H4'), the mean of C(T) only the credit (H5'). No full 2-round collision is exhibited. The submitted program is that of entry 26ebba63, unchanged (the earlier sub-class search, its own constants). This search's member, outcome set, budgets, credit, lanes, pre-check, (G7), solver layout and certificate are defined in proof.md only.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, the beta* cube (beta*, mask, value), the seven tau values and eps of the filter's automata and the mask of S are what the search reads (73 bytes); the program also stores the two sub-class bits and the rule-A words of its root instance (93 bytes of advice in all). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by one exact count per model; beta* is the beta of that solution, and S has the least exact charge of the 16,383 nonempty outcome sets. preprocessing_log2 55 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 (below 2^62.946 operations) in full and is included in time_log2: the search alone is below 2^66.7956 units, the selection below 2^54.198. That the selection returns these values rests on records and a stated, unproved operation-rate bridge. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, selection and search, all held at once (sum below 2^44). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Over the run's RUN_STEPS independent uniform 256-bit words, let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, and an E1 outcome in S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, six outcomes of beta*; Y4 in the whole class of eta; no rule on h1), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter or the pre-check. (i) E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = FACTOR * 2^-128, FACTOR = floor(5 * 138,512,695,296 / 7) = 98,937,639,497, about 2^-91.474 (just under five sevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1 for S). (ii) The probability that no valid trial of the run is a listed good trial is at most exp(-0.49676) + 0.001. Given (i), rho = E[N_o(N_o-1)]/E[N_o] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8. This restates the rate-and-dependence premise of entry 26ebba63 for the whole class and S; that entry's accepted clause was for the sub-class of 2^17 members with rule A and seven outcomes and does not by itself imply this law: equal model counts and equal budget constants do not identify the law of N_o, and rho need not be the same (GPT Sol, answer AT 2). It is declared here anew. By Lemma F every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, and by Lemmas VP and G7 the pre-check and the guard (G7) skip no listed good trial, so N_o is the same count, pointwise (GPT Sol, answers AW 1 and AX 1); the rate per member of Q* of a passing outer step is q / pi_o, about 2^-81.496 if pi_o equals the exact share pi.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 a member of the whole class of eta (524,288 values, Lemma Q) drawn with the outer words from the run's fresh 256-bit words (seven outer steps to a batch, each on its own disjoint bits, Lemma PL), E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 in every trial, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 for S are searched further, and only those that the pre-check of 9.7 keeps reach the solver; N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step and only the six outcomes of S.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10 with Y4 uniform in the class, of the part of beta* on the class carried by the six outcomes of S (67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 on the per-trial scale 2^-83 of the class; the counting program and the six rows of its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1), taken at five sevenths, rounded down. The filter, the pre-check and the guard (G7) change neither the count nor the premise (Lemmas S9 (b), VP and G7). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: a whole-class graphics-card run of 2^46 real counter trials in 2^25 passing outer steps, with a sub-class control of the same size, in which every measured quantity matches the exact model within 1.5 clustered standard errors, among them the E1 rate on the whole class of the seven outcomes of entry 59f8915e, 1.0020 +- 0.0086 of the model (13,595 events), and its ratio to the sub-class rate, 0.9895 +- 0.0120 (model 1); that counter covered the seven together, so the E1 event of S is a sub-event of the measured event (52/53 of it in the model) and was not counted on its own; 2^43 real trials inside passing outer steps of the seven-outcome filter on the sub-class, listed E1 outcome 0.979 +- 0.022 of its value; and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages, with no sub-class and no rule, in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 98,937,639,497 is assumed (five sevenths of the model count of the six outcomes of S on the class, rounded down). The accepted premise of entry 26ebba63 was for the sub-class with rule A; it is not inherited, and the whole-class law of N_o for S is declared, not proved. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. The transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is partly proved (Lemmas S1-S5, S8, S9, VP and G7) and partly assumed in (i); the weak-dependence condition of (ii) is assumed, with a proved cap of 32 listed good trials in one outer step (Lemma CV). The whole-class graphics-card run measures the E1 side of the seven outcomes together and the filter, not the six of S on their own, not the E3 side (N3 four times that of the sub-class) nor the joint event, and its trials lie in passing outer steps of the fourteen-outcome filter, a superset of this filter's. Lemmas F, VP and G7 and Lemma S9 (a) use no law of the words; the 8-bit end-to-end run has no filter.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. Two count-budget clauses with one failure allowance for their union: with probability at least 0.9995 over the coins both hold, so no budget halts the run. (a) Pass budget: at most PASS_BUDGET = 858,218,304,486,124,116 outer steps pass the filter for S (nominal share pi = 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782). (b) Lean test-(2) budget: at most E_BUDGET = 47,103,299,361,697,960,684 lanes have a test-(2) mask meeting S and run the Q path (nominal share 233,715,456 / 2^32 = 2^-4.1998). Each budget is ceil(17/16 * RUN_STEPS * share). Reaching a budget halts with failure; the time bound charges each budget plus one. The number of outer steps that reach the solver has no budget and no clause here: the solver is paid from the credit of H5prime-weighted-solver-work (GPT Sol, answer AW 5, which keeps these two count halts and replaces the third by the credit).
heuristics.scope: The counts N_E and N_2 of proof.md 10.3 over the RUN_STEPS outer steps of step 1 of Section 9.1, with Y4 drawn from the whole class: each is binomial over independent outer steps (Lemma PL) with the sampler's probability of its indicator; the two indicators of one outer step may depend on each other in any way.
heuristics.extrapolation: The nominal shares are exact for uniform independent (Y9, omega) (GPT Sol, answers AC, AN and AW 3; the certificate of Section 8). If each sampler probability is at most 1.06 times its nominal share, the Chernoff bound puts each overflow below exp(-RUN_STEPS * share * 53 / 18,020,000): exp(-1.3 * 10^14) and exp(-2 * 10^12), so their union is below 2 * exp(-2 * 10^12), far below 0.0005. Measured (Section 13, untrusted by the harness, Python's generator, whole class): on 60,000,000 real outer steps the two counts are 1.0004 +- 0.0005 (test (2)) and 0.9980 +- 0.0041 (pass) of their nominal values; on another 30,000,000 the pass count is 0.9981 +- 0.0058 of its nominal value. With the seven-outcome filter on the sub-class the pass share was 1.00012 +- 0.00016 of its exact value on 2^35 outer steps.
heuristics.limitations: That each sampler probability is at most 1.06 times its nominal share is not proved: the sampler's Y9 and omega are not proved independent and uniform. The measurements are runs of one generator made after the design, not a locked validation. The time bound, the filter and the pre-check do not depend on these shares.

heuristics.statement: Supporting (GPT Sol, answers AW 5 and AX 1: the premise H4-AS-v-S(eps), E_phys[V_S(U)] <= (1+eps) * cbar_S, at eps = 0.06, for the solver with the guard (G7)). For an outer step U of the run, before any halt, let V(U) = C(T(U)), where T = X AND VMASK[nu] is the set of outcomes that the pre-check of proof.md 9.7 keeps and C is the proved cap of steps 2 and 3 with the guard (G7) for those outcomes (the restricted ledger 4,096 + 2,304 F + 1,280 A + 20 N_f + 48 N_r + 4 N_s + 368 Lf over the rows of T without the free position 7, Section 11; at most 31,456), with V(U) = 0 when T is empty or the step does not pass the filter. Premise: under the sampler, E[V(U)] <= 1.06 * cbar, with cbar = 582,173,006,981,436 / 2^47 = 4.136588..., the exact mean of V in the counting model. It is one weighted moment over all outer steps, zeros included; it is not a mean of executed work, since V bounds the work of steps 2 and 3 in every outer step. Use: before steps 2 and 3 the run debits C(T) from CREDIT = ceil(17/16 * RUN_STEPS * 1.06 * cbar) = 3,795,525,293,015,084,470,051 and halts with failure when C(T) exceeds the remaining credit; under the premise, with independent outer steps (Lemma PL) and 0 <= V <= 31,456, the Bernstein inequality puts the probability that the credit is exhausted below exp(-2.1 * 10^14). The time bound charges the whole credit and does not depend on the premise; success 0.39 holds under H1', H4' and this premise (proof.md 10.4).
heuristics.scope: The values V(U) of the RUN_STEPS outer steps of step 1 of proof.md 9.1, each a function of the outer step's own random word (Lemma PL), with Y4 drawn from the whole class of eta, S = 0x005f, the masks X of the filter of Section 8 and nu by formula (V) of 9.7; the mean is over all outer steps, passing or not.
heuristics.extrapolation: cbar is exact in the counting model M_v of proof.md 10.3: uniform independent (Y9, omega), as for the nominal shares of H4', and an independent uniform three-bit nu; cbar = sum over the masks A and nu of n_A C(A AND S AND VMASK[nu]) / 2^51 = 582,173,006,981,436 / 2^47 = 4.136588... (GPT Sol, answers AW 5 and AX 1; rebuilt in integers from the program's own automata). Measured (proof.md Section 13, untrusted by the harness): on 2^25 = 33,554,432 real outer steps of the whole class (32 SHA-256-derived seeds), V = C(T) with (G7) had sum 136,173,472, sample mean 4.058286 against 4.136588 (ratio 0.98107 +- 0.01126, z = -1.68), largest value 31,456, and one-sided empirical Bernstein upper bound 1.03053 (delta 0.00135, range 31,456), below 1.06; and on an earlier preregistered sample of 2^28 = 268,435,456 real outer steps without (G7) (PREREG.txt SHA-256 c862bfb1082e5236b0d9d81d6daef38e5f1135b27b25ad5c0093a1bf76455872), the ratio to its model mean was 0.99456 +- 0.00405 with one-sided upper bounds 1.01059 (empirical Bernstein) and 1.01513 (bounded KL), also below 1.06.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: the sampler's nu is a function of the outer step and is not proved uniform or independent of the masks, so the model value cbar is not a property of the sampler. The sample is statistical evidence from one pseudorandom generator, run by the participant and not by the organizer's harness, on the counter instance that no organizer experiment runs; it supports eps = 0.06 and not eps = 0.0095. It does not test H1' or the two count clauses of H4'. If the premise fails, the credit can halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound. This premise takes the place of the third count budget of entry 0bc5f130 of the same participant.
